title: Optimal Viewing Window Selection for Polynomials
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a suitable viewing window [x_min, x_max] by [y_min, y_max] that clearly displays all local extrema, intercepts, and inflection trends of the cubic polynomial f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 2.

steps.title: Analyze Polynomial Behavior and Extrema
steps.explanation: Critical points occur at x = -1 and x = 3. Evaluating f gives f(-1) = (-1)^3 - 3(-1)^2 - 9(-1) + 2 = 7 (local maximum) and f(3) = 3^3 - 3(3)^2 - 9(3) + 2 = -25 (local minimum).
steps.why: Local turning points establish the minimum required vertical span of the graph.

steps.title: Analyze y-Intercept and Inflection
steps.explanation: The y-intercept is at (0, 2), and the inflection point lies at x = 1, y = -9.
steps.why: The central feature coordinates must fall well inside the window margins.

steps.title: Select Symmetrical Margins
steps.explanation: An x-span of [-4, 5] captures both critical values x = -1 and x = 3 with sufficient room to observe end behavior. A y-span of [-30, 15] accommodates the minimum at -25 and maximum at 7 with comfortable margins.
steps.why: A standard viewing window should include all critical points plus 20-30% boundary margins.
